key_insight: SeasonStereo makes dense stereo matching more robust to seasonal and illumination changes in multi-date satellite images. It aims to enable reliable 3D reconstruction even when stereo pairs are not captured at the same time.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of estimating accurate disparity from diachronic satellite imagery, where images taken on different dates have different appearance due to season, lighting, and scene changes. Existing stereo methods struggle because large-scale aligned training data and ground-truth geometry are expensive to obtain.
method: Uses a scalable generative-AI-based framework to synthesize or leverage training data for multi-date stereo robustness.
Trains a dense stereo matching model specifically to handle appearance variation across dates instead of assuming near-simultaneous image pairs.
Focuses on disparity estimation for satellite imagery in diachronic settings, improving generalization to real-world seasonal and illumination shifts.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it expands dense stereo to far more realistic remote-sensing scenarios, including historical reconstruction and monitoring over time. It can reduce the dependency on costly manual ground truth and make 3D mapping from satellite archives more practical.

paper_title: SeasonStereo: Robust Dense Stereo Matching for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery via Generative AI
